races.paceDynamic: Diamond Exchange is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the outset, likely setting a sustainable tempo without serious pressure through the early stages. Dutch Gold and Day Trader may track prominently but neither appears keen to challenge for the lead. With 10 of 13 runners adopting hold-up tactics, the pace will be steady early before quickening from the 3f pole as the large pack of closers fan out. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace, as the wall of hold-up horses will struggle to find racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Sets Up Perfectly
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange maintains a steady gallop to halfway then quickens
scenarios.body: The front runner gets first run while prominent trackers like Dutch Gold can follow the move before the hold-up brigade get organized. Those within striking distance at the 2f pole hold decisive positional advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large group of hold-up horses encounter significant interference turning for home
scenarios.body: Multiple runners get hampered or forced wide, allowing the most capable closers with clear runs to capitalize. Abbey Actress and Diego El Queso possess the class to navigate trouble and finish strongest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Folds Late
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange sets too strong a pace or stops in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The pace collapses completely, bringing every hold-up horse into contention in a messy finish. The best horse on ratings among the closers prevails in a tight photo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and tactical awareness proves decisive
scenarios.body: A lightly-weighted runner like Switch From Diesel or an improving sort gets the perfect trip on the rail. Fresh legs and tactical positioning overcome superior ability in a surprise result.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Exchange sets the tempo alone - if the pace becomes too slow early, every hold-up horse comes into play
Traffic problems at the 2f pole with 10+ hold-up horses converging simultaneously on a narrow track
Abbey Actress for market support given her soft ground record and recent form revival
Dutch Gold and Day Trader tracking positions behind Diamond Exchange through the first half-mile
Switch From Diesel for fitness levels after 164-day absence, any market confidence would be significant

races.paceDynamic: Mississippi River and Norwalk Havoc will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over this straight mile at Leopardstown. Their honest pace will stretch the field and create a true test of stamina, particularly on the yielding ground which will sap energy reserves. The strong early gallop will suit those with tactical speed who can travel prominently rather than those relying on finishing kicks from the rear. This pace scenario strongly favours prominent racers and those with proven stamina at the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Benefits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Mississippi River and Norwalk Havoc set genuine fractions and maintain the tempo
scenarios.body: The strong pace will find out the stamina-shy and set up perfectly for those racing handy to the pace. Horses like Mutasarref and Expanded, who can sit prominent and have the class to quicken, will benefit from the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters get away with softer fractions than expected
scenarios.body: Mississippi River or Norwalk Havoc could capitalise on their forward positions if the pace becomes more sedate. Their early advantage would prove decisive if the closing kick from behind fails to materialise on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too strong and burns out the leaders completely
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop could set up perfectly for the patient hold-up performers to sweep past tired leaders. The Lion In Winter and Lord Massusus have the class to benefit from a pace collapse in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a messy tactical affair with uneven pace
scenarios.body: A stop-start tempo could bring improvers like Tokenomics and Ribee into contention against classier but rustier rivals. The yielding conditions would aid their stamina while others struggle with the tactical nature.

watchPoints.text: If Mississippi River and Norwalk Havoc go too fast early, they could set it up for the hold-up horses despite the tactical disadvantage
Mutasarref has home advantage with four course wins but hasn't quite reached 2024 levels this season
The Lion In Winter's hold-up style needs the anticipated strong pace to be fully effective
Several runners face significant layoffs over 150 days which could blunt their fitness edge
The yielding ground will emphasise stamina and could favour those with proven form on similar surfaces

races.paceDynamic: Some Good Men Gone appears the only natural front runner in this field and will face minimal pressure early. The prominent runners (Teffian Warrior, Urban War, Staywitherjohnny, Baila Conmigo) are likely to settle behind while the hold-up horses (Zipster, Star Mind, Tyraxes, Your Out Of Line) drop further back. With one unchallenged leader and a small field, this sets up a moderate tempo that could quicken late. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can track the pace and strike, penalising pure hold-up horses who need a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Some Good Men Gone gets an easy lead and kicks clear
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows him to dictate fractions and use his best weapon - front running ability. His second at Naas off a higher mark suggests he has the class to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes steady and suits those tracking
scenarios.body: Zipster's hold-up style could work if he gets close enough, while Tyraxes has shown good recent form when getting his conditions right. The moderate tempo allows them to stay in touch and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Fails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow for hold-up horses to make impact
scenarios.body: Star Mind and Your Out Of Line need a stronger gallop to be effective but won't get it with one uncontested leader. Their finishing kicks will be blunted by the tactical nature of this small field contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Some Good Men Gone stops quickly and creates a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: Multiple horses could benefit from a pace collapse including any prominent runners who stayed close. This low-probability scenario would need the leader to hit a wall completely.

watchPoints.text: Some Good Men Gone could steal this if allowed an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home

races.paceDynamic: Thru And Thru is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate a sustainable tempo without early pressure. However, seven horses (Glory To Be, Free Solo, I Bid You Ajou, Chester Nimitz, Vega's Muse, Verhoyen, Thaloria) want prominent positions, creating significant traffic congestion turning for home. The large field of hold-up horses (Greek Flower, Anvika, Pebble Island, Amemri, Goal Exceeded, Senna's Girl, Finsceal Annie, Hugo's Girl) will be looking for gaps 2-3 furlongs out. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can secure early position and avoid the inevitable traffic jam that will trap the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Position Gold
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses avoid early scrimmaging and secure clear positions behind Thru And Thru
scenarios.body: The seven prominent racers get first run on the field while hold-up horses meet trouble in running. Those with tactical speed to sit handy but not lead will have ideal positioning when the pace quickens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Special
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates a messy pace with multiple horses fighting for position
scenarios.body: The bunching allows a patient hold-up horse with the best turn of foot to weave through and strike late. Only the classiest closers will have the acceleration to overcome the positioning disadvantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Thru And Thru gets an uncontested lead while the field argues behind
scenarios.body: The front-runner builds an unassailable advantage as the field neutralizes itself with positional battles. By the time the field organizes a challenge, the leader has stolen too much ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is very modest and Thru And Thru crawls along in front
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 3f pole where raw speed trumps position, allowing horses with natural pace to overcome poor draws or positions.

races.paceDynamic: Romantic War is the sole committed front-runner and will dictate terms from the gate, likely getting an uncontested lead in the opening stages. Seven horses targeting prominent positions (She's Ideal, Sedro Woolley, Twotolose, Rock Basher, Brains, Mullacash Buzz, Jazzy Dancer) will create serious traffic problems turning for home as they all converge on limited rail space. The large field of hold-up horses (Zabriskie Point, Roman Harry, Mogwli, Methgal, Cannonball Queen, Kitty Bear, Sea Fort, Exceeding, Chipsrdown) will be relying on the pace to collapse and gaps to appear late. This race shape strongly favours early pace - either the uncontested leader or those who can secure clean prominent positions without getting caught in the squeeze.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic War gets an easy lead and the prominent pack neutralise each other
scenarios.body: The front-runner will have too much in reserve when the traffic-delayed closers finally get clear running. Multiple hold-up horses will flatten out after expending energy navigating the congestion.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Escape Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If one or two prominent runners secure clean positions outside the rail squeeze
scenarios.body: These horses will have first run on the weakening leader while the hold-up brigade are still stuck behind the wall of traffic. The clean travellers will kick clear before the late runners can mount their challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Through Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to stop Romantic War and gaps appear for closers
scenarios.body: The prominent pack will come back to the field after pressuring each other, allowing the patient hold-up horses to capitalise with late runs. Fresh legs will tell in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic War stops dramatically and all prominent runners fade together
scenarios.body: The entire front division will come backwards as one, creating a cavalry charge finish from the rear. Multiple hold-up horses will hit the line together in a blanket finish.
